cell.label: Suspected opioid overdose. Also consider hypoglycemia, stroke, and co-ingestion of other abused drugs. Assess respiratory rate and oxygenation.
Bag-mask ventilation with supplemental O2. Give naloxone 0.1 mg IV boluses (or 0.4 IM or 0.8 SC if no IV access) with escalating dose titration until RR ≥10. Long- or short-acting opioid?
Consider IV naloxone at 2/3 of effective bolus dose/hour. Admit and continue for 12-24 hours. If RR <10 after 10 mg administered, consider alternative diagnosis.
Naloxone 0.05 mg IV boluses (or 0.4 IM or 0.8 SC if no IV access) until RR ≥10. Success?
If RR <10 after 10 mg administered, consider alternative diagnosis.
Observe at least 2 hours prior to discharge. Worsening respiratory status or recurrence?
Observe at least 2 hours. Worsening respiratory status?
Consider discharge with close follow-up versus continued observation.
Repeat naloxone boluses as above until RR ≥10.
